The hearing was presided over by **NTR District Collector Dr. G. Lakshmisha**, with representatives from various organizations participating. The Human Rights Forum (HRF) strongly opposed the project, demanding the cancellation of the Draft Environment Impact Assessment (EIA) Report due to errors.

recent_articles.title: KMRL offers measures to ease traffic snarls as monsoon nears - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Kochi Metro Rail Limited (KMRL)** has implemented several measures to improve road safety and traffic management along the Kakkand route ahead of the monsoon season. The company will deploy additional traffic wardens, install reflectors and reflective tapes on barricades, realign barricades for better driver guidance, and gradually remove barricades as construction progresses. **KMRL** also directed its contractors to undertake comprehensive monsoon preparedness activities at construction sites and ensure drains are cleared to prevent flooding.

recent_articles.title: Summer showers, strong winds damage over 200 houses in Ernakulam - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Heavy summer showers** in Ernakulam district have caused widespread damage, with **201 houses** damaged between March 1 and May 17 this year compared to only 15 houses damaged during the same period last year.  The intense rainfall led to tree uprooting, waterlogging, and damage to agricultural land, causing estimated crop losses of ₹6.92 crore across 2,306.62 hectares. **District Collector G. Priyanka** stated that village officers are conducting assessments and compensation will be provided to affected parties.

recent_articles.title: Supreme Court declines to interfere with forest clearances for Adani’s Madhya Pradesh coal block project - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Supreme Court** declined to intervene in environmental clearances granted to the Adani Group's coal block project in Madhya Pradesh. The court noted a delay in challenging the approvals and observed that the National Green Tribunal (NGT) had relied on a 2025 ruling regarding limitation periods for challenges.  While the petitioner argued for judicial review of the clearances due to environmental concerns, the **Adani Group** urged dismissal of the plea. The court suggested Mr. Dubey pursue other legal remedies and granted him liberty to do so.

recent_articles.title: Hot weather on the cards during Eid as PMD predicts heatwave from May 25-31 - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Pakistan's** **Meteorological Department (PMD)** has issued a heatwave warning for the country from May 25 to May 31, with temperatures expected to reach 47-50°C in some areas. The federal government has declared a three-day public holiday from May 26-28 to allow citizens to stay safe during the extreme weather conditions. **The PMD** advises the public to take precautions against heatstroke and conserve water and electricity.

recent_articles.title: Sacred hall housing Japan's 'eternal flame' destroyed by fire
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A fire destroyed the Reikado Hall on Miyajima island, causing significant damage to the Daishoin Buddhist temple complex. The **Japan Times** reports that the hall housed the "eternal flame," which has been burning for nearly 1,200 years and was moved to a different location after the fire. Authorities are investigating whether the blaze may have been caused by the flame itself, as the hall also burned down in 2005.

recent_articles.title: Feral horse numbers surge in Kosciuszko national park after pause in aerial culling, survey shows | New South Wales | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **New South Wales** government data shows feral horse numbers in **Kosciuszko national park** surged to between 6,476 and 16,411 in late 2025, a sharp increase from the previous year.  The surge prompted calls for urgent action from conservation advocates who argue that retention zones allowing thousands of horses to remain in the park should be scrapped. **Penny Sharpe**, NSW environment minister, acknowledged the need for continued management but emphasized the government's commitment to reducing feral horse numbers to 3,000 by mid-2027.  The Invasive Species Council chief executive, **Jack Gough**, called for amendments to the feral horse management plan and urged the government to eliminate retention zones altogether.

recent_articles.title: Suo motu case against top Karnataka officials after raids expose illegal sand mining in Bagalkot - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Lokayukta Police** in **Karnataka** have registered a suo motu case against several senior government officials, including the Director of the Mines and Geology Department in Bengaluru and the Bagalkot Deputy Commissioner, for alleged large-scale illegal sand mining in the Krishna river bed. The investigation followed complaints about rampant illegal mining activities in Bagalkot district and revealed indiscriminate excavation using heavy machinery in violation of environmental norms.  The **Lokayukta Police** conducted raids across Bagalkot district on May 21, seizing equipment and uncovering large quantities of illegally extracted sand.  Further investigations are underway to determine the extent of the illegal activity and hold those responsible accountable.

recent_articles.title: Record number of dams dismantled in Europe in effort to help wildlife thrive | Rivers | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Iceland** removed its first official dam from a river in 2025, joining other European countries in a growing trend of barrier removals. **Dam Removal Europe**, an environmental group coalition, found that over 600 barriers were dismantled across the continent last year, with **Sweden**, **Finland**, and **Spain** leading the way. The removal of these structures aims to restore natural river flow and wildlife habitats, but researchers caution about potential risks from invasive species.  The EU's nature restoration law explicitly calls for the removal of obsolete dams, as does a similar effort in the US.
